FINDING: app/auth.py:14 | security | high | `find_user` builds SQL with an f-string from the caller-supplied name, so it is open to SQL injection (including an authentication bypass via `check_login`).
FINDING: app/auth.py:5 | security | high | `SECRET_KEY` is hardcoded in source, so anyone with repo access can forge signed tokens.
FINDING: app/files.py:10 | security | high | `export_report` joins the caller-supplied filename into `EXPORT_DIR` without sanitizing it, so an absolute path or `../` allows writing files anywhere.
FINDING: app/orders.py:13 | logic | high | `apply_discount` uses `>` where the docstring says "$100.00 or more", so an order of exactly 10,000 cents gets no discount.
FINDING: app/orders.py:23 | logic | high | Tax is computed on the undiscounted subtotal, but the docstring says it should be charged on the discounted amount.
FINDING: app/inventory.py:10 | logic | high | The slice end `start + page_size - 1` is off by one, so each page returns `page_size - 1` items.
FINDING: tests/test_inventory.py:7 | tests | high | `assert len(page) <= 10` passes even when the page is short, so it cannot catch the pagination off-by-one.
FINDING: tests/test_orders.py:21 | tests | high | `test_discount_at_threshold` only prints the result and asserts nothing, so it cannot catch the `>` versus `>=` bug.
FINDING: app/orders.py:62 | logic | medium | `place_order` ignores the return value of `reserve` and checks stock per line, so duplicate SKUs can oversell and a partial failure is not atomic.
FINDING: app/auth.py:21 | security | medium | The username is used as the PBKDF2 salt, so the salt is predictable and not unique per user; a random stored salt should be used.
FINDING: app/orders.py:37 | performance | medium | `dedupe_skus` tests membership against a list, which makes it O(n²); use a set alongside the ordered list.
FINDING: tests/test_orders.py:25 | tests | medium | No test covers a discounted order with tax, so the tax-on-undiscounted-subtotal bug goes undetected.
FINDING: tests/test_auth_files.py:14 | tests | medium | `test_find_user` uses only a benign name, so it cannot detect the SQL injection, and it never checks the not-found case.
FINDING: app/auth.py:9 | security | low | PBKDF2 runs only 100,000 iterations, below current recommendations of about 600,000 for SHA-256.
FINDING: app/auth.py:35 | security | low | The token is an HMAC of only the user_id with no expiry or nonce, so an issued token is valid forever and can be replayed.
FINDING: app/orders.py:46 | performance | low | `count_by_status` rescans every order once per status; a single pass would do.
FINDING: tests/test_inventory.py:20 | tests | low | `test_reserve_success_and_failure` never checks that stock was decremented on success or left unchanged on failure.
FINDING: tests/test_auth_files.py:18 | tests | low | `test_sign_token_is_stable` would pass with any deterministic function, because it never checks the actual HMAC value.
FINDING: tests/test_auth_files.py:25 | tests | low | The report round-trip test uses only a plain filename, so the path-traversal behavior of `export_report` versus `read_report` is untested.

The bug-hunter flagged the print-only test at line 19 and the test-reviewer at line 21. I used line 21, where the `print` is. The bug-hunter also noted it did not read `tests/conftest.py`.
